mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 4.48% (a level that is currently observed) is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as historically when rates are at this level, the market has shown a tendency to rise in the short term.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in the current rate environment are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns, as higher rates compress equity valuations and increase the cost of capital.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and the CPI index (indicating monetary tightening amid high inflation) predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 returns, as the dual pressure compresses both equity valuations and real economic activity.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rising) does not produce negative returns in > 60% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 320 (indicating high inflation), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns, as high inflation erodes real earnings and increases uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 320, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (the 2017 base index), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns, as a contraction in manufacturing and services signals an impending economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day forward returns, as high unemployment signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300.0 thousand units, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns, as strong housing activity indicates a robust economy and rising consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in < 40% of instances when HOUST > 1300.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) predicts positive 5-day S&P 500 returns, as strong housing demand amid manufacturing weakness signals a shift to consumer-driven growth that benefits equity markets.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (HOUST rising and INDPRO falling) does not produce positive returns in > 60% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
